contexts.text: Pleasures ... thus ... partake ... of heavenly happiness.
The more the worship (then) partakes of the world, the body, and the earth; and the less of the spirit.
In proportion as they cannot participate, or have hope of participating, (in this worship of self), they are disunited.
For all his work partakes of the evil which is within it.
God is wisdom itself, of which man is the partaker.
That ye be not partakers of her sins () = that they should beware lest they be as to their souls conjoined with these abominations...
He represented to himself that the innocent were partakers with him.
To be partakers, when said of sins, = to come into them, and thus to become guilty of them.
Therefore the speech of men in each word partakes of space, time, and what is personal and material.
